newsitem.title: INDIA: India wants early talks with Pakistan - president.
newsitem.headline: India wants early talks with Pakistan - president.

text.p: India is committed to improving relations with Pakistan and hopes for the early resumption of bilateral peace talks, President Shankar Dayal Sharma said on Thursday.

"With Pakistan, we are committed to ending confrontation and establishing a harmonious relationship and durable peace, as provided for in the Shimla Agreement," Sharma said in a speech prepared for delivery to parliament at the start of its budget session.
In the 1972 Shimla Agreement, India and Pakistan pledged to resolve their differences through peaceful means in bilateral negotiations.

"We believe that fostering people-to-people contacts and promoting trade and economic links will contribute to this process," Sharma said in his speech, which had earlier been cleared by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet.
"We are ready for dialogue with the new Government of Pakistan and hope for an early resumption of talks," the Indian president said.

On Tuesday, Deve Gowda said in a letter to Pakistan's new prime minister, Nawaz Sharif, that India wanted to resume peace talks which broke down in early 1994, and was willing to discuss a wide range of issues including disputed Kashmir.
